Scenarios.Scenario: Open a Markdown file using one of the newly listed extensions in the normal text editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Editor resolution performs the two contributed custom-editor glob checks, but both editors have textEditor priority `option`, so neither custom editor is selected automatically. The normal text editor can proceed without creating either webview. Markdown extension activation/language-server startup is already caused by the existing `markdown` language association for these extensions, not by this diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Starts one Markdown language-server worker over IPC when the built-in Markdown extension activates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one client/server instance per extension activation, shared across Markdown documents rather than one per file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening these suffixes already assigned language id `markdown` through extensions/markdown-basics/package.json and therefore could activate the same Markdown extension and server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This may occur when the Markdown language activates, but all newly selected suffixes were already contributed as language `markdown`; the selector expansion does not add or move this boundary onto the path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One resource URI per editor-open resolution. The brace expansion adds a constant 13-suffix match to each of two existing selector checks; it does not scan workspace files or scale with workspace size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous constant-count selector matching; no new queue, fan-out, or concurrent boundary work is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The custom-editor contribution is loaded and stored as before. No new cache key, miss path, negative cache, or invalidation behavior is introduced; only the two selector strings change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the manifest priorities and resolver schema explicitly state that `option` editors are not automatically used, and the existing language contribution already covers every added suffix.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact cost of parsing the longer glob is not measured, but it is two constant-size matches per resolved resource and has no realistic multiplicative input.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Normal opens gain only negligible constant selector matching and do not construct a webview or add boundary work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Explicitly use Reopen With to open an alternate-extension Markdown file in Markdown Preview
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the user explicitly selects the preview editor (or configures that exact editor association), the provider resolves one text document, creates one webview, and renders the Markdown before the preview is usable. This heavyweight work is the requested feature path and remains off the normal-open path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activates the Markdown extension and starts its shared language-server worker if it is not already active.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared server on cold extension activation, not one per preview or suffix.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The language server and preview machinery already existed for `.md`; the added suffixes were already Markdown language files, while the custom preview was not offered for them by this selector.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold activation must complete before the custom-editor provider is registered, but these files already activate the extension through their existing Markdown language association in the usual open workflow.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Creates and wires a webview-backed static preview and sends rendered content/messages to it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One webview per explicitly opened preview editor, with refreshes governed by the existing preview lifecycle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This explicit custom-editor path was not offered by the manifest for the added suffixes; users of `.md` already incurred identical work when selecting the preview.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first render is on the explicit preview-open critical path; it is not triggered merely because a matching file exists or opens normally.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The webview may load local or remote resources referenced by the rendered document under existing preview security/resource-root rules.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Driven by references in the one explicitly previewed document and browser/webview caching, not by the count of matching workspace files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The manifest did not expose this preview for the added suffixes; the same resource loading already occurred for explicit `.md` previews.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Referenced resources can affect preview completeness after initial HTML rendering, but this is existing requested preview behavior.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with the opened document size and referenced preview resources, one preview instance per explicitly opened editor. There is no loop over all files with one of the new suffixes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One provider resolution per explicitly opened editor. Existing preview refresh and webview messaging behavior is unchanged; the diff adds no burst, limiter bypass, or per-item fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The shared Markdown engine/contribution provider remains reused across previews; webview/local-resource caching and refresh behavior are unchanged. Cold first open pays existing activation/render setup, while warm opens reuse the activated extension.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the selector now makes this editor available, while `option` priority proves it is not auto-selected. The provider trace shows one webview/render lifecycle per selected preview.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Document size and resource counts vary, but the expensive work is gated by an explicit editor choice and has unchanged per-preview behavior.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The newly reachable work is exactly the explicitly requested preview feature, with bounded per-editor cardinality and no added repetition or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Explicitly use Reopen With to open an alternate-extension file in the hybrid Markdown Editor, including diffs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An explicit choice resolves the custom text editor, creates a scripted webview, and configures it with the document. Diff use is also optional (`diffEditor: option`) and creates the existing one-panel inline or two-panel side-by-side layout only after selection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Creates a webview, injects editor HTML, and exchanges document/update/provider messages with the webview.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One webview per explicitly opened editor panel; side-by-side diff can use two panels. Message content scales with the selected document and edits, not all matching files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The manifest did not offer this custom editor for the added suffixes; `.md` files already used the identical provider path when explicitly selected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Webview setup is required for the explicitly selected hybrid editor but absent from normal text-editor opens.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reads contributed code-block editor resources or explicitly requested URI-backed content when those features are used.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per resolved contributed provider/resource request within the selected document, with existing provider promise/resource caches; not per matching workspace file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These conditional reads were reachable only when the custom editor was selected for previously matched files; their frequency and caching are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Conditional feature work, generally after base webview creation; unchanged by the selector apart from explicit availability for more Markdown suffixes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Initial serialization/rendering scales with the selected document size; code-block provider work scales with providers and code blocks in that document. Retained state scales with the number of explicitly open custom-editor tabs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One resolve flow per opened panel; document edits are serialized by the existing `editQueue`. Provider API promises/maps coalesce existing resolution work, and the diff changes none of these controls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The provider caches resolved code-block editor APIs/resources in existing maps for the activated extension lifetime. `retainContextWhenHidden` preserves each explicitly opened webview as before; selector expansion does not alter eviction or cleanup semantics.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both text and diff priorities are `option`; provider code shows existing per-panel webview ownership, serialized edits, and cleanup. The diff only broadens the eligible Markdown suffixes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large documents or many retained custom-editor tabs can be costly, but the diff does not auto-open them or change the existing retention lifecycle, and prevalence depends on explicit user selection.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Costs are intentional, explicitly initiated custom-editor costs, with unchanged per-document scaling, coalescing, and lifecycle.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete one-file, two-hunk diff and traced normal opens, explicit preview opens, hybrid-editor opens, and diff opens through editor resolution, extension activation, webview IPC/serialization, conditional filesystem/resource loading, caches, concurrency, and cleanup. The longer selectors add only constant matching to normal opens; all heavyweight work remains gated by optional/explicit editor selection. No actionable performance regression was introduced.
